note: THE GIT STASH STACK IS SHARED ACROSS EVERY WORKTREE, AND IT CURRENTLY HOLDS FIVE CAMPAIGNS PARKED WORK. A bare git stash pop from any session takes whatever is on top, which is very unlikely to be yours. Observed 2026-09-06 from campaign/the-newel: an implementer stashed a pre-edit baseline, and by the time it went to restore, another sessions entry had appeared ABOVE it. git stash list at that moment read -- stash@{0} campaign/the-grammar preserve parked Task 2 partial; stash@{1} campaign/the-kerf task5-review-fix-crash-recovery; stash@{2} campaign/the-zenith Task 8 interrupted partial work; stash@{3} campaign/the-wash WIP; stash@{4} campaign/the-planes timings rows. Five campaigns, five parked stashes, one stack. THE MECHANISM: git keeps the stash reflog in the COMMON git dir, not per worktree, so every linked worktree shares one stack. Nothing about git worktree add isolates it. WHAT TO DO INSTEAD: capture the stash SHA when you create it and restore with git stash apply SHA then git stash drop SHA -- never a bare pop, never a bare apply. Better still for the common case of checking what a test did before your edit: git stash create does NOT push onto the shared stack at all, and git show SHA:path diffed against your tree touches no shared state whatever. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT SOUNDS: the loss is silent and asymmetric. The session that pops gets a successful-looking restore of someone elses work onto its own tree; the session that parked the work finds its stash gone with no error, possibly hours later, possibly after a compaction that removed its memory of having stashed at all. Two of the five entries above are explicitly labelled interrupted or parked partial work, which is exactly the material that is not reconstructible from a report. CREDIT: the Task 6 implementer noticed this unprompted and restored strictly by matched SHA, leaving the other four untouched.
